title: Gas-Liquid Separator

introduction.definition: A two-phase separator splits a mixed stream into gas and liquid. The inlet device breaks the momentum, liquid drops out by gravity, a mesh pad catches fine mist near the top, and a level control valve keeps the liquid at the right level.

introduction.summary: A gas–liquid separator splits a mixed stream into gas and liquid. The inlet device breaks the momentum, liquid drops to the bottom by gravity, and a mesh pad near the top catches fine mist before the gas leaves. A level controller and control valve keep the liquid level constant.

video_tutorials.title: Gas-Liquid Separator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Gas-Liquid Separator.
A two-phase separator splits a mixed stream into gas and liquid.
The inlet device breaks the momentum, liquid drops out by gravity, a mesh pad catches fine mist near the top, and a level control valve keeps the liquid at the right level.
Typical applications include production separators (oil & gas); compressor suction scrubbers; flash drums; steam/water separation.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Gas-Liquid Separator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gas-Liquid Separator.
Check level control and ΔP across mesh.
Calibrate level instruments.
Inspect/replace mesh pad.
Watch for liquid carry-over: liquid in gas line. Common cause: high gas rate, plugged/damaged mesh, high level.
Watch for gas blow-by: gas in liquid line. Common cause: low level.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
